To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we were able to crawl 1.2 billion web pages written in Latin and 0.8 billion written in Cyrillic script, that we were able identify 0.5 billion web pages written by Bosnian, 0.6 billion by Croatian and 0.7 billion by Serbian speakers, that we were to identify 0.1 billion pages written in other closely related languages and that we were able reduce the amount of low-quality data to 0.3 billion pages.

we were able to: (1) construct a web corpus of 2.4 billion words in three languages with a high degree of purity, (2) identify language of the documents written in two scripts with a high degree (99.5%) of accuracy, (3) identify low-quality documents in the web corpus with an accuracy of 98.6% and (4) outperform the state of the art on the task of discrimiating between three languages.

1. the proposed language identification method based on language models trained only on crawled data outperforms state-of-the-art classifiers on the task of discrimating between closely related languages, 2. the proposed method is suitable for constructing web corpora of closely related languages and 3. the constructed corpora contain low quality data which is identified and filtered out using language models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.

a number of problems that are common to all top-level-domain web corpus construction processes and that have not been addressed so far, namely the simultaneous crawling and processing in two scripts, the identification of documents written in the closely related languages and the removal of low-quality documents.
the construction and cleaning of a web corpus for three closely related languages, and the application of a language modeling technique for both tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have constructed a corpus that is suitable for the majority of research and application purposes, but it still requires further manual processing to be used for more sensitive tasks.
our approach is not a silver bullet, but a valuable addition to the existing tools.
we have constructed the first web corpus for each of the three languages, which is suitable for the specific purposes of the research and applications that we have in mind.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

by using the presented approach we have built a corpus that contains more than 1 billion tokens, which is the largest publicly available corpus of Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, and which is of higher quality than the previous largest corpora of the same size.
we show how to construct a web corpus for a language with two scripts, how to discriminate between closely related languages and how to filter out low-quality data from web collections.
we show how to build a large web corpus of three closely related languages with a relatively high quality and with a minimal human intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of language models for language identification is a promising direction for web corpora of closely related languages.
the language modeling approach can be successfully applied to web corpora in closely related languages and can be used to identify and remove the noisy data in the corpus.
it is possible to construct a high-quality web corpus with the help of language modeling only and that it is possible for the corpus to be used for research on closely related languages.
